## 0. Working title and one-paragraph story
**"How much shorter can a prediction-powered interval be? Headroom over PPI++ when labels, unlabeled data and the predictor are all fixed."**

Prediction-powered inference (PPI, PPI++) turns a fixed predictor into a valid interval for E[Y]. With n labels, N unlabeled records and f fixed, the only freedom left is (a) how the labels are used to build the control variate g(Z), and (b) how the interval is built from the estimate. The classical semi-supervised / missing-data theory gives a variance floor V* = σ²_res/n + V_g/(n+N). We (1) write the exact gap between PPI++ and that floor, (2) say when learning a calibrated g from the same n labels pays for itself (break-even n*), (3) measure the headroom on the nine ppi-python sets, a synthetic suite with known truth, and (4) map where shorter intervals exist, where they do not, and where any method fails. We claim no new efficiency principle and no "first" (Zhang–Brown–Cai 2019; Robins–Rotnitzky–Zhao 1994; Gronsbell et al. 2022 are credited).
